findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Pick one canonical term for the 'neither none nor paths' scope kind (either 'unscoped' or 'undeclared') and use it consistently in Approach, Testing, and the Acceptance Criteria; update the other occurrences to match.
evidence: Classifier contract: 'empty paths classify as unscoped'
Safety interlock: 'material_fingerprint keeps the legacy basis byte-for-byte for undeclared and paths scopes'
Testing: 'material_fingerprint differs across undeclared / none / paths'
AC6: 'A pre-feature attestation lacking file-scope: retains its current validity' — described as 'undeclared' in Testing but 'unscoped' in classifier contract
findings.finding: The plan uses 'unscoped' and 'undeclared' to name the same scope kind in different sections, creating a terminology inconsistency an implementer must resolve by guessing. Approach classifier section and Context use 'unscoped'; the safety-interlock paragraph, Testing bullets, and AC6 use 'undeclared'.
findings.location: Approach ('Classifier contract' paragraph and 'safety interlock' paragraph), Testing section, AC6
scenarios: An implementer writing classify_file_scope must decide whether the return value string is 'unscoped' or 'undeclared', and whether the manifest line (if any) would use the same token — the plan gives both spellings.

findings.suggested_fix: Standardize on 'unscoped' (the term used in the classifier contract, which is the primary interface definition). Update 'undeclared' in the safety-interlock paragraph, Testing bullets, and AC6 to 'unscoped'. Reserve 'undeclared' only if it refers specifically to the legacy state of a manifest that predates this feature (i.e. a manifest with no file-scope: line), in which case distinguish 'unscoped' (classifier return value) from 'undeclared' (reader result for legacy manifests) explicitly.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit post-rollback state assertion to the plan: state that `none`-scope attestations signed under new code will yield `stale-material` on rollback (due to the fingerprint declaration-marker change), forcing re-review, and confirm this is the intended/acceptable conservative behavior with no data loss.
evidence: Plan states: 'A rollback leaves additive file-scope: none manifest lines ignored by old readers, while new readers treat a missing line as undeclared.'
Plan states: 'Only none adds a canonical declaration marker containing no_file_impact_reason.'

ABSENCE: no assertion about what happens to the `material_fingerprint` mismatch when old code re-evaluates a `none`-scope attestation signed by new code — old `material_fingerprint` would omit the declaration marker, producing a different hash than the signed one, yielding `stale-material`.
T11 criterion requires: 'the plan must assert on the schema STATE AFTER rollback, not merely that rollback exits 0'
findings.finding: The plan's rollback description covers only the manifest line ('old readers ignore file-scope: none') but does not assert the full post-rollback validity state for attestations signed under new code: (1) old readers silently falling through to whole-HEAD stale-head is conservative/safe but unasserted; (2) more critically, `material_fingerprint` is changed to include a canonical declaration marker for `none` scope — a `none`-scope attestation signed under new code carries a fingerprint old code cannot reproduce, so rollback would cause `compute_validity` to return `stale-material` for those attestations rather than `certified`. The plan must affirmatively state the post-rollback state (forced re-review for `none`-scope tickets signed during the new-code window) and confirm no data loss occurs.
findings.location: Approach section, paragraph: 'The safety interlock is the material fingerprint … Only `none` adds a canonical declaration marker containing `no_file_impact_reason`.' and 'A rollback leaves additive `file-scope: none` manifest lines ignored by old readers'
scenarios: Deploy new code; some tickets are reviewed and signed with `file-scope: none` and the new declaration-marker fingerprint. Roll back to old code. Old `compute_validity` recomputes `material_fingerprint` WITHOUT the declaration marker → hash mismatch → `stale-material` verdict on all previously-certified `none`-scope attestations. These tickets now require re-review, which is conservative/safe but constitutes operational disruption that the plan does not acknowledge.

If a rollback is performed during active use, any `none`-scope attestations that were `certified` become immediately invalidated by the fingerprint mismatch — a form of forced re-review that the plan should document as the known rollback consequence.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to the Approach rollback paragraph: 'On rollback, `none`-scope attestations signed by new code yield `stale-material` because old code recomputes `material_fingerprint` without the declaration marker — this forces re-review (conservative/fail-closed) and is the intended behavior. No attestation data is lost; affected tickets simply require a fresh plan-review pass under the old code.'

findings.finding: The plan introduces a new tri-state attestation scope kind (`none` / `paths` / `unscoped`), a new `file-scope:` manifest line format, a new `classify_file_scope` helper contract, and a modified material-fingerprint basis — all constituting an architectural decision. The project already cites ADR 0049 for the related authenticated-manifest-only rule, establishing a pattern of capturing attestation architectural decisions in ADRs. No ADR creation or update is mentioned in the plan's Scope section.
findings.location: Approach section; Scope section; Acceptance Criteria
scenarios: A future maintainer modifying `compute_validity` or `build_manifest` has no normative reference for why the tri-state exists or what invariants must be preserved
If S3 or S4 extend the scope system, they have no ADR to amend, leading to undocumented behavioral drift
The backward-compatibility contract (missing `file-scope:` line = undeclared) is a durable invariant that belongs in versioned documentation
findings.suggested_fix: Create `docs/adr/NNNN-attestation-file-scope-tristate.md` covering: (1) the three scope kinds and their semantics, (2) the `file-scope: none` manifest line format and authenticated-only read rule, (3) the material-fingerprint differentiation rationale, (4) the backward-compat invariant for legacy manifests. Reference this ADR from the Scope section of the plan.
